articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: NASA needs more recruits in order to return to the moon after being gone more than half a century.
articles.title: NASA is looking for astronauts to live and work on the Moon

articles.author: Willem Marx
articles.description: France says European officials will attend this week's U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round of negotiations since February.
articles.title: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who will lead a caretaker government while negotiations take place, said: "I think everyone's over politics so let's all have a bit of a break for the next three weeks".
articles.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: On Sunday, tens of thousands packed the main square in Florida, Uruguay, to watch Pope Leo speak.
articles.title: After a successful trip to Uruguay, Pope Leo heads to Argentina

articles.author: Kate Bartlett
articles.description: Comedian Brand faces a "significant" prison sentence, which a London court judge is set to hand down on Monday.
articles.title: Russell Brand to learn sentence after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault

articles.author: Connie Hanzhang Jin
articles.description: From Arctic landscapes to insect bodies, climate change is shifting the familiar colors of nature.
articles.title: Climate change is altering the colors we see in the world: an illustrated journey

articles.author: Elaine Appleton-Grant
articles.description: Air medical service comes with high risks, high costs, and staffing struggles. To reduce turnover and serve rural patients, LifeFlight of Maine is putting the needs of healthcare workers first.
articles.title: One air ambulance service rethinks what it takes to practice medicine in the sky

articles.author: John Bartlett
articles.description: El Niño rains have transformed Chile's Atacama Desert into a spectacular sea of color, awakening a fleeting ecosystem of flowers and wildlife in one of the driest places on Earth.
articles.title: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades

articles.author: Elena Moore
articles.description: Republicans made gains with young voters in 2024, but in this year's midterms Americans under 30 issued a strong rebuke of President Trump and his party, voting decisively for Democrats instead.
articles.title: How Gen Z voters helped fuel a blue wave for Democrats

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: President Donald Trump said Sunday he was only kidding about making UFC boss Dana White his next White House press secretary
articles.title: Trump says he was just kidding about making UFC's Dana White his press secretary

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
‘It’s pretty obvious that there are all sorts of people making all sorts of comments,’ Murray Watt says after budget savings meeting

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The environment minister, Murray Watt, has urged ministers to stop undermining the treasurer, Jim Chalmers, as Labor struggles to sell its budget and looks to cut popular clean energy subsidies to help with the fight against inflation.
Cabinet ministers met again on Monday to discuss potential budget savings to be included in next month’s mid-year update, part of efforts to reducing spending to ease pressure on the economy.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stop undermining Jim Chalmers, environment minister urges Labor colleagues

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Minister says Labour hoping to offer bed to every rough sleeper in England but cites chronic housing shortage
Andy Burnham’s pledge to tackle rough sleeping by getting “everyone in for Christmas” is in jeopardy amid rising numbers of people on the streets and a severe housing shortage.
Official figures show an increase of nearly 1,000 people sleeping rough in England between January and June, the latest month for which figures are available.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham’s homelessness pledge to ‘get everyone in for Christmas’ in jeopardy

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Coffee shop chain targets growth north of London with extra 500 outlets in big boost for youth employment
Starbucks has set out plans to hire 7,500 new baristas over the next five years, in a boost to youth employment as the chain pins hopes for future growth on the north of the country.
The US coffee shop chain, which employs more than 18,000 people in the UK, said the hiring spree would focus on the Midlands, north of England, Wales and Scotland, as it targets growth north of the M25.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Starbucks plans to hire 7,500 staff in major UK expansion plan

articles.author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
articles.description:
Ben Carroll refuses to be drawn on latest opinion poll that puts Labor at all-time low of just 18%, behind One Nation on 21% and the Coalition on 33%

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Victorian Labor MPs are both sceptical and seriously concerned about a new poll ahead of the state election showing the party trailing third behind One Nation, with its primary vote at an all-time low of just 18%.
The DemosAU/PremierNational, first published by the Herald Sun on Monday, showed Labor’s primary vote share has crashed seven points to 18%, putting it in third place behind the Coalition’s 33% and One Nation’s 21%. At the same time, the Greens improved their primary vote to 17%, an increase of three points since September.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Victorian election 2026: Concern and scepticism among Labor MPs as new poll shows party trailing One Nation

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
President makes unusual acknowledgement that one of the defining policies of his second administration had become a political liability
Donald Trump has admitted that his deportation policy was “too tough” and has offered to strike an immigration deal with Democrats in a concession following the Republicans’ disastrous defeat in the midterm elections.
In an interview on the CBS network’s 60 Minutes broadcast on Sunday, the president acknowledged that the aggressive crackdown had hurt him politically and said he was open to an arrangement to allow some undocumented immigrants to remain in the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump tells 60 Minutes that deportation policy was ‘too tough’

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Roberto Urbano, 51, appears in court via video link after death of 47-year-old Feng Jianming in the CBD on Friday night

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A food delivery rider’s alleged murderer has pulled down his pants and exposed himself as he appeared in court.
Roberto Urbano, 51, appeared in Melbourne magistrates court via video link on Monday after being charged with murder and intentionally causing serious injury.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man accused of HungryPanda delivery rider’s stabbing murder yells and exposes himself in Melbourne court

articles.author: Anne Davies
articles.description:
Chris Minns and race discrimination commissioner lambast comments made by Stuart Bonds, who leads party’s NSW upper house ticket

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales premier and the Australian Human Rights Commission have criticised comments by the man who heads One Nation’s upper house ticket in NSW after he said Australians faced demographic replacement unless “mass migration” was curtailed.
Chris Minns described Stuart Bonds’ comments as “frankly outrageous and racist”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Outrageous and racist’: premier responds to NSW One Nation candidate’s claim Australians are being ‘demographically replaced’

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Pontiff tells Argentina’s president the economy must benefit all on second stop of 12-day Latin America tour
Pope Leo XIV has delivered a stinging critique of Argentine president Javier Milei’s harsh austerity measures, insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause in Buenos Aires.
“The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy,” he said on Sunday, shortly after landing in Argentina on the second leg of a Latin America tour.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pope Leo delivers stinging rebuke of Milei’s austerity measures during Argentina visit

articles.author: Kat Wong and Ima Caldwell
articles.description:
Former police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington in early 2024

Warning: This article contains graphic content

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon has told a Sydney court he did not “execute” Jesse Baird as he acted out the way he allegedly shot the 26-year-old.
The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I never executed Jesse Baird’: Beau Lamarre-Condon re-enacts shooting when giving evidence in NSW trial

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
President says it was ‘just a little fun’ to picture White, UFC boss and Trump’s friend, in briefing room with fighters
Donald Trump said on Sunday that he “was only kidding” when he announced a day earlier that he had offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC).
Speaking to reporters on his way back the White House from his beach club in Florida, Trump explained the premise of his joke, that if the UFC boss, who is a devoted fan of the president, took over the briefing room, flanked by six fighters, reporters “wouldn’t mess around with him so much”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about making UFC’s Dana White next press secretary

articles.author: Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
‘Time to throw myself into something new,’ 32-year-old presenter announces on social media while hailing her ‘unforgettable time’ on the show
Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of Love Island after three years.
The 32-year-old presenter of the reality TV show made the announcement on Instagram.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Maya Jama steps down as Love Island host after nine seasons

articles.author: Marina Dunbar and Robert Mackey
articles.description:
CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing
Nvidia said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”.
The New York Times reported in ​October that Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence that Huang ‌had a close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence

articles.author: Richard Adams Education editor
articles.description:
Lucy Powell says proposals to end widespread practice will be included in overhaul of England’s national curriculum 
Pushing GCSE subjects on younger pupils risks turning England’s secondary schools into “early exam factories”, the education secretary has said, warning that it is increasing disengagement from education.
Lucy Powell wants schools to end the widespread practice of teaching GCSE topics to pupils in year 9 or earlier, before they officially start in year 10, and says she plans to reduce the amount of GCSE content to make it easier to fit into the official timetable.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Teaching GCSE topics younger risks turning schools into ‘early exam factories’, Powell warns

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
£40m scheme in England aims to keep most vulnerable people well at home and avoid unnecessary hospital stays 
Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable patients in England are to receive extra support from their GP as part of a £40m drive aimed at keeping them out of hospital this winter.
As the NHS gears up for the pressures of the coming months, family doctors will offer 300,000 people with frailty and long-term conditions health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests designed to prevent avoidable hospital admissions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: GPs to offer 300,000 patients extra support to ease winter strain on NHS

articles.author: Angela Giuffrida
articles.description:
Jakub Kulik critically injured and Artur Morański also wounded after actions that ‘prevented further casualties’
Two Polish police officers who were injured as they pursued and detained the gunman in Kraków on Saturday have been hailed as heroes.
One of them is Jakub Kulik, a former paratrooper and volunteer firefighter, who was left critically injured after a close-range exchange of fire with the suspect, a 24-year-old Polish national who killed six and injured 17 in an attack believed to have been inspired by far-right ideologies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two police officers hailed as heroes for confronting Kraków gunman

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell
articles.description:
Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary candidates in Tuesday’s elections, report says
The US midterm elections saw voters elect a slew of historic representatives – from the country’s first Muslim senator to the first Black female governor – but among the most significant gains were those for Native American women.
On Tuesday, voters elected the first Native American woman governor, senator and leaders of two tribal nations. Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary and Two Spirit candidates in the November midterms, according to Advance Native Political Leadership and the news site ICT.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Seismic shift’: Native American women made significant gains in US midterms

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Man taken to hospital after falling off Royal Caribbean ship in Pacific Ocean, with Coast Guard investigating incident
A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two Newport Beach, California, fishermen discovered him treading water in the Pacific Ocean nearly 20 miles (32km) offshore on Friday.
The unidentified man was taken to the hospital after the rescue, according to the US Coast Guard, which is now investigating how he went overboard from the cruise ship.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued after nine hours treading water miles from shore

articles.author: Keely Aouga
articles.description:
No one was injured after emergency landing in Fort Myers 50 minutes after takeoff with two people onboard
A small plane crashed into the rear of a pickup truck as it made an emergency landing on a busy Florida highway on Saturday but miraculously no one was injured in the dramatic incident.
Video footage obtained from the sheriff’s office shows a Cessna 172 grazing over the truck as it approached the ground for a complete landing on a road in Fort Meyers at about 11.45am on Saturday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Small plane crashes into pickup truck on busy Florida highway

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
Culture secretary pushes back against talk of revisiting Brexit but says closer ties would fulfil referendum promises
One of Andy Burnham’s cabinet ministers has said she wants to avoid “circular arguments” about whether the UK should rejoin the EU, underlining divisions at the top of government over revisiting Brexit.
Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, appeared to suggest she was not in favour of rejoining the trade bloc, but she said the prime minister should still pursue closer ties to fulfil the promises made at the time of the referendum.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lisa Nandy wary of ‘circular arguments’ about rejoining EU

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Former military chief says prime minister brought Israel to historic crisis and it is approaching ‘point of no return’
Israel’s former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task of forming a government on Sunday, reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu’s allies as he said the veteran prime minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.
Eisenkot, 66, the leader of the Yashar party, who has vowed to bridge Israel’s deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from the president, Isaac Herzog, who gave him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gadi Eisenkot reaches out to Netanyahu allies as he strives to form government

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo
Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Bailiffs reportedly seized digital records before court case over alleged intellectual property breaches on Land Rover Defender
Bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover raided the Dutch offices of a Chinese “copycat” rival before a legal showdown this week over whether its “Defender clone” infringes intellectual property rights.
Bailiffs acting on behalf of JLR reportedly seized digital records from the offices of Chinese carmaker BYD in Schiedam and Hoofddorp in August, according to the Sunday Times.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Knesset has been deadlocked since the election last month when Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition lost its majority
Israel’s president has ⁠chosen Gadi Eisenkot, the prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ⁠strongest rival, to ⁠try to ​form a new government, after a deadlocked election that left neither man ⁠with a clear path to power.
Isaac Herzog’s office said he had informed Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, on Saturday night “of his intention to task him with forming a government”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israel’s president picks Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot to form government

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll and Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Five of seven facilities in England and Wales never reached operational stage as Tories vacillated over plans to check goods
The UK wasted at least £100m in taxpayers’ money to set up zombie Brexit border inspection posts that were never used, it has been revealed.
The overall cost of Brexit was put at an estimated £4.7bn by the National Audit Office last year but this included years-long transformation of the software used for customs declarations and other systems built to cope with the UK leaving the single market.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK spent £100m on zombie Brexit border inspection posts

articles.author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
articles.description:
See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives
African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.
See My World, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester

articles.author: Angela Giuffrida and agencies
articles.description:
Six people killed in attack probably inspired by far right, according to officials, as police say suspect’s parents and sister found dead at his home
Polish prosecutors have opened a terrorism investigation after a 24-year-old man opened fire in a busy market square in Kraków, killing six people including a Briton and injuring 17, in an attack that authorities said was probably inspired by far-right ideologies.
Police confirmed on Sunday that three people found dead at the gunman’s home after the attack on Saturday afternoon were his father, 53, mother, 52, and sister, 21.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Polish prosecutors open terrorism investigation into Kraków shooting

articles.author: Facundo Iglesia in Buenos Aires
articles.description:
President has opposing views on many issues, and once called Leo’s predecessor the ‘representative of the Evil One’
Trees are being planted in the garden. The brightly coloured buildings are getting another coat of paint. The choir rehearses. Hundreds of other residents, several of them using wheelchairs, practise their positions outside the sanctuary. Excitement is in the air, because on Monday 9 November, the Cottolengo Don Orione – a Catholic-run home for disabled people – will be the first stop on Pope Leo XIV’s first full day of his trip to Argentina.
But the pope’s visit to Claypole, about 26km from Buenos Aires, does not come at an especially happy time for the home, which counts about 400 residents with disabilities. Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has made wide-ranging cuts to disability funding.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pope’s visit to Argentina sets up showdown with ‘hyper-capitalist’ Milei

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event
Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event.
High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body. In the Dominican Republic, farmers are expected to face drought conditions, with forecasts of drier and warmer than usual conditions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Banana producers in Latin America want better pay to cope with effects of climate crisis

articles.author: Rebecca Ratcliffe, Gloria Dickie and Elisângela Mendonça
articles.description:
Mumbai facility is part of Reliance Industries, owner of world’s biggest oil refinery and funder of controversial mega-zoo
The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will host its forthcoming annual awards ceremony at a venue owned by the billionaire Ambani family conglomerate, drawing criticism from conservationists over their fossil fuel businesses and their foundation’s controversial mega-zoo.
A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which awards £1m to five winners every year to invest in conservation work, confirmed to the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay that this year’s ceremony will be held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on 17 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Environmentalists criticise choice of Earthshot prize venue owned by fossil fuel firm

articles.author: Amy Hawkins
articles.description:
Activists fear Bangkok will give in to pressure from Beijing despite reports of torture and human rights abuses against the mostly muslim ethnic minority
The deportation of two more Uyghurs to China from Thailand would put their lives in grave danger, activists have said, with one of the men saying he would be “like a slave” if he was sent back.
Last year, Thai authorities forcibly deported 40 Uyghur men to China despite pleas from the men themselves and the UN.
 

 

 The US and Canada had reportedly offered to resettle them, but Bangkok appeared to want to avoid upsetting Beijing. The UN has said the returnees’ whereabouts remain unknown.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Uyghurs facing deportation by Thailand say they will be ‘like slaves’ in China

articles.author: Eva Corlett in Auckland
articles.description:
National party will be largest in parliament but ultimate shape of next government won’t be settled for some time
New Zealand could be facing a weeks-long wait to know the shape of its next government, after its nail-biting election failed to hand a decisive victory to either the incumbent rightwing coalition or opposition left bloc.
On preliminary results, the centre-right National party, led by the prime minister, Christopher Luxon, managed to secure enough seats to govern alongside its traditional coalition partners, the libertarian Act and populist New Zealand First parties.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NZ election 2026: New Zealand faces weeks of uncertainty with results ‘too close to call’

articles.author: Mark Saunokonoko
articles.description:
This blog is closed, you can read our report on the New Zealand election here

Another update here with 8% of the vote counted.
 

 

 National on 31.2%, Labour 28.4%, the Greens 12.9%, Act 11.2%, NZ First 9.6%, Opportunity 5.7% and Te Pāti Māori 0.4%.
On these numbers, we would have a right bloc coalition back in power. Long way to go.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New Zealand election coalition talks will likely take weeks – as it happened

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Department had claimed that being kidnapped for ransom was not exploitation of trafficking victims in case of Syrian man abducted in Libya
The court of appeal has rejected claims by the Home Office that being kidnapped for ransom is not exploitation of trafficking victims.
The ruling means that many people who have been kidnapped for ransom, whom officials have previously excluded from being victims of exploitation under trafficking rules, will now have to have these claims considered. They may be eligible for the support and recovery package trafficking victims are entitled to.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Court rules against Home Office in asylum seeker kidnapping case

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Trump still considering new assault on Iran nuclear sites – though threats less credible after Vance remarks
Qatar, the lead mediator in the US-Iran conflict, is seeking to persuade Tehran to allow UN nuclear weapons inspectors to visit Iran’s bombed nuclear sites, including those housing the country’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium.
Iran would not be required to make any commitment that the stockpile would be removed from the country, with other options on the table, including reducing the uranium content by down-blending it.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Strait of Hormuz could reopen as part of Qatari plan for Iran nuclear inspections

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Democrats’ sweep could urge Israel’s divided opposition to join forces and remove prime minister closely allied with Trump
The Democrats’ sweep of Congress may make it easier for Israel’s splintered opposition to overcome deep internal divisions and form a coalition government, by increasing the urgency of unseating Benjamin Netanyahu, who has associated himself so closely with Donald Trump’s Republicans.
But as Israel took stock of the results, there was also a sense that the elections marked a longer-term shift in US politics that will make the job of any new Israeli leader far more difficult.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US midterm results may help unite Israeli coalition to unseat Netanyahu

articles.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
articles.description:
Santiago Peña was detained minutes after he was impeached by Congress, as protesters took to the streets demanding answers after the suspension of the Ueno bank
Paraguay’s rightwing president has been placed under house arrest minutes after he was impeached by Congress, amid a severe crisis that left more than half the country’s population unable to access their bank accounts.
Santiago Peña is being investigated about allegations he used his political influence to favour a bank that expanded exponentially under his government and was suspended this week after irregularities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ousted Paraguay president under house arrest after banking crisis leaves 60% of country unable to access accounts

articles.author: Mark Sweney and Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
Asian and European markets follow US tech rout with many analysts predicting more waves of selling to come
European and Asian stock markets fell sharply on Friday after the Democrats’ decisive victory in the midterms triggered a rout in US tech stocks a day earlier.
A sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday was followed by sharp falls in Asian stock markets on Friday. The investor sentiment then reached London, where the market was, at one stage, poised for its worst day since March.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Global stocks fall amid ‘big worries over AI’ after Democrats’ midterms triumph

articles.author: Benjamin Lee
articles.description:
The Chilean film-maker, whose films starred Florence Pugh, Julianne Moore and Rachel Weisz, died at his home in Santiago
Chilean film-maker Sebastián Lelio has died at the age of 52.
He was best known for the Oscar-winning trans drama A Fantastic Woman and his English-language films included Gloria Bell and The Wonder.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sebastián Lelio, director of A Fantastic Woman and Gloria, dies aged 52

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families
The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.
The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result
The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.
Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted

articles.author: Sarah Johnson
articles.description:
Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit
A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed.
“A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday. “The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British healthcare worker with Ebola evacuated from DR Congo to UK

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
A previously unseen family archive offers a glimpse into the Indian Nobel prize winner’s artistic process and personal relationships in his final years

Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

It’s easy to run out of words to describe Rabindranath Tagore. The first non-European to win the Nobel prize in literature, Tagore was a Bengali poet, musician, novelist, philosopher, songwriter, painter, humanist and educator.
Born in 1861, Tagore left an indelible mark on the subcontinent’s literature, music, education and art. Among his enduring legacies are the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The private creative world of Rabindranath Tagore, the man Yeats called ‘greater than any of us’

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield, Elisângela Mendonça and Phoebe Weston and Spoorthy Raman
articles.description:
Guardian and Mongabay reveal approaches to officials and MPs on behalf of  Vantara zoo ahead of UK-chaired Cites meeting on endangered animal imports

British government ministers were told not to engage formally with Vantara, the controversial mega-zoo run by the Indian billionaire Anant Ambani, after lobbying efforts by the private animal sanctuary in the run-up to a UK-chaired meeting on the trade in endangered species, according to documents.
This week, the UK heads a 32-country committee meeting in Geneva of Cites, the United Nations body that regulates trade in endangered species. The meeting will examine how India has responded to compliance concerns about imports of endangered animals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK ministers told not to engage formally with Indian mega-zoo after lobbying

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Led by Congress party, India’s opposition alliance channels anger over removal of 130 million names from voter roll
Thousands of opposition supporters have gathered in Delhi as protests against the Narendra Modi government continue to gather momentum.
Led by the Congress party, India’s opposition alliance has brought together supporters from across the country, amid growing anger over a large-scale revision of the country’s voter roll that has seen 130 million names erased.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tens of thousands protest against Narendra Modi regime in Delhi

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
Rubio’s decision not to meet Narendra Modi last week was seen by some as a snub – but by focusing on business leaders and oil, the secretary of state made American priorities clear. Plus: the artist bringing a female perspective to men’s clothing
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
When the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, visited India for the second time this year, headlines concentrated on who he met and where he went.
The fact that Rubio bypassed New Delhi and did not meet the prime minister, Narendra Modi, during his trip last week, and instead traveled to the financial capital, Mumbai, where he met India’s foreign minister, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar (pictured top with Rubio), and business leaders, did not go unnoticed. Nor did his decision to travel to Jamnagar, the small Gujarati town that is home to Reliance Industries’ colossal oil refinery complex.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What Marco Rubio’s sidestepping of New Delhi says about the US’s stance on India

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
President makes unusual acknowledgement that one of the defining policies of his second administration had become a political liability
Donald Trump has admitted that his deportation policy was “too tough” and has offered to strike an immigration deal with Democrats in a concession following the Republicans’ disastrous defeat in the midterm elections.
In an interview on the CBS network’s 60 Minutes broadcast on Sunday, the president acknowledged that the aggressive crackdown had hurt him politically and said he was open to an arrangement to allow some undocumented immigrants to remain in the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump tells 60 Minutes that deportation policy was ‘too tough’

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
President says it was ‘just a little fun’ to picture White, UFC boss and Trump’s friend, in briefing room with fighters
Donald Trump said on Sunday that he “was only kidding” when he announced a day earlier that he had offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC).
Speaking to reporters on his way back the White House from his beach club in Florida, Trump explained the premise of his joke, that if the UFC boss, who is a devoted fan of the president, took over the briefing room, flanked by six fighters, reporters “wouldn’t mess around with him so much”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about making UFC’s Dana White next press secretary

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell
articles.description:
Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary candidates in Tuesday’s elections, report says
The US midterm elections saw voters elect a slew of historic representatives – from the country’s first Muslim senator to the first Black female governor – but among the most significant gains were those for Native American women.
On Tuesday, voters elected the first Native American woman governor, senator and leaders of two tribal nations. Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary and Two Spirit candidates in the November midterms, according to Advance Native Political Leadership and the news site ICT.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Seismic shift’: Native American women made significant gains in US midterms

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
House Democrat is a ‘hard yes’ on impeachment resolution against defense secretary who ‘has abused his power’
House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, poised to become majority leader, said on Sunday that he strongly supports impeaching defense secretary Pete Hegseth as a Republican lawmaker prepares to force a House vote.
The top Democrat made his position clear during an appearance on ABC’s This Week, declaring himself a “hard yes” on the impeachment resolution targeting Hegseth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hakeem Jeffries supports impeachment of Pete Hegseth: ‘He has got to go’

articles.author: Zach Vasquez
articles.description:
SNL booking comedian Druski post-midterms felt misbegotten in low-energy episode failing to capture historic ‘blue-nami’
Four days after the historic “blue-nami” midterms, Saturday Night Live opens at Democrats’ headquarters, where party leaders Hakeem Jeffries (Kenan Thompson) and Chuck Schumer (Sarah Sherman) celebrate, even as they vow to hold on to power in spite of the wishes of their energized base.
Their toast is interrupted by the man responsible for Republicans’ shellacking, Donald Trump (James Austin Johnson). The president, who is “now lame duck”, accepts the results, “which is scarier in a way”. But he’s also resigned to focus on the ballroom, even as he laments having to work with millennial Democrats (this leads him down a long diatribe about the show New Girl). We get quick walk ons by a defeated JD Vance (Jeremy Culhane) and extra-aggro Pete Hegseth (Colin Jost), only for Trump to get a taste of his own medicine when James “Telefreako” Talarico interupts him. Texas’s new senator-elect speaks to one of the big issues of the day: “It’s clear people want something new, they want something different. I’m talking, of course, about SNL’s cold opens. How many of these Trump freezes are they gonna do?”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saturday Night Live: Druski hosts and James Talarico cameos, but where’s the post-election comedy?

articles.author: Ted Widmer
articles.description:
Tuesday’s winners offered a new politics at a time when ‘there is something broken in America’
As the US election returns came in throughout the night on Tuesday, there was ebullience at the size of the margin. It was comparable to the significant thumpings over the years. Yet bigger.
In 2006, Americans were exhausted by the war in Iraq (by simply changing the last letter to “n”, we have a similar situation today). But even that big win paled in comparison.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The light of dawn is on the horizon’: the best moments from US midterm victory speeches | Ted Widmer

articles.author: Heba Gowayed
articles.description:
The blue wave, while a rebuke of Trump’s policies, was also a referendum on the party’s status quo
On election night I stood in a crowd at Harlem Tavern, a restaurant in New York City, at the electoral party for Darializa Avila Chevalier, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) member and congresswoman-elect from New York’s 13th congressional district. The crowd cheered as what came to be called the “blunami” rolled in: Iowa blue, Kansas blue, Talarico in Texas, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, House, Senate, gubernatorial races overwhelmingly going for the Democratic party.
The victories were a clear rebuke of Trump’s politics, but also a referendum on the Democratic party’s own centrism that is complicit in the violence of masked men hunting immigrants, the funding of a genocide and the denial of healthcare to citizens of the world’s wealthiest country.
Heba Gowayed is an associate professor of sociology at CUNY Hunter College and Graduate Center and author of the book Refuge: How the State Shapes Human Potential.
 
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Centrism did not win the Democratic party the election

articles.author: Chris Stein in Washington
articles.description:
Midterms success gives party potent leverage over Trump – expect tough campaigns of investigating and lawmaking
“Costs, chaos, corruption”: after almost two years spent relentlessly criticizing Donald Trump for failing to address those three, broad political concerns, Democrats won a monumental return to power in Tuesday’s midterm elections that will give them potent new leverage over the president.
Now the question becomes: what will they do with it?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healthcare, tariffs – but not Trump impeachment: Democrats chart next two years of power

articles.author: Lex McMenamin
articles.description:
After helping Trump to victory in 2024, young voters swung decisively toward Democrats, helping deliver a wave of midterm victories
The 2026 blue tsunami owes a lot to the youth vote.
According to data from Tufts University’s Center for Information & Research on Civic Learning and Engagement (Circle), which monitors youth civic engagement, early estimates show the second-highest youth turnout in a midterm election in 30 years, second only to 2018, when an estimated 31% of young voters turned out during Donald Trump’s first presidency.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘People are active, they are fed up’: young voters fueled the Democratic wave

articles.author: Isabeau Doucet in San Francisco
articles.description:
Voters approved two measures to save the region’s financially distressed public transit agencies
Voters in the San Francisco Bay Area overwhelmingly approved two transit measures this week that advocates hope will save the region’s financially distressed public transit agencies from a potential death spiral that could have had massive repercussions for the area’s residents and its economy.
The Regional Transit Measure (RTM), a 0.5% sales tax across four Bay Area counties and a 1% sales tax in San Francisco, will generate approximately $1bn annually to fund the region’s four largest transit operators. It received a strong 62.2% support across all five counties that voted on the measure, winning with a landslide of 78.6% in San Francisco.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Did the Bay Area just save its transit system from the brink of certain death?

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
The ‘secretary of war’ and his shameful history are facing bipartisan scrutiny
Can you smell the schadenfreude in the air?
Watching some of the worst people in the world get their comeuppance this week has been deeply satisfying. And the show isn’t over yet. While the midterms have wrapped up, the blame game is only just getting started, with Republicans desperate to find scapegoats for their shellacking.
Arwa Mahadwi is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Will Pete Hegseth be the blue tsunami’s next victim? | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Saida Grundy
articles.description:
Maga’s regret voters were all-in for Trump’s racism. Then they found out they couldn’t afford it
For the first time in a decade, election predictions far exceeded public expectations. What pollsters anticipated as a blue wave billowed into a blue tsunami. Wins that held ground for already blue seats eased nerves, and the flips of swing states such as Georgia, North Carolina and Ohio – and the victory in Michigan – energized the blue base. But red-belt-busting wins in Republican strongholds like Texas, South Carolina and Kansas alongside pending races in Alaska and Mississippi left mouths agape. The explanation was that Democrats turned out far more supporters than their regulars, and that the “regret voter” (both swing voters and partisan Republicans) expanded the wave across districts Tru…
articles.title: Flip voters discovered that Trump’s racism and xenophobia are expensive

articles.author: Sam Levin
articles.description:
From North Carolina to Arizona, Democrats with almost no public profile were stunned at their election triumphs
One candidate had dropped out in September. One had no campaign staff. One was a 19-year-old and halfway through the fall college semester.
Across the US, Democratic candidates with almost no public profile and long odds of winning their midterm races were stunned to find they had outperformed their opponents on Tuesday. They were swept into Congress and statehouses in the blue wave that knocked out Republicans from seats considered untouchable in deep-red districts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Wait, what?’: the underdog Democrats who won their midterm races against all odds

articles.author: David Smith, Laure Boulinier, Naomi Schanen, Karif Wat, John Farrell and Sarah Bertram
articles.description:
Democrat James Talarico won a Senate seat in Texas, breaking a 38-year drought for his party in the Republican stronghold and delivering a stunning blow to Donald Trump. The race became one of the most expensive Senate contests in US history, with advertising spending topping $500m, according to estimates. GOP-aligned groups poured hundreds of millions of dollars into efforts to elect Ken Paxton, including substantial funding linked to multibillionaire Elon Musk, whom Talarico accused of trying to buy a Senate seat.


Elon Musk’s nearly half a billion dollars in midterms spending was a flop

Five dimensional chess: inside James Talarico’s extraordinary bid to break Texas Democrats’ losing streak

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Texas v Musk: how southern state Democrats won against the billionaire – explainer

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland , produced by Danielle Stephens and Nada Smiljanic
articles.description:
Jonathan Freedland hosts a live panel to look at what happens next – for Donald Trump, the Republicans who might want to succeed him, and for Democrats looking ahead to 2028. He is joined by the Guardian’s Washington bureau chief, David Smith; Tara Setmayer, a co-founder and CEO of the Seneca project; the Guardian’s global editor, Devika Bhat; Adam Smith, a professor of US politics and political history at the University of Oxford; and the clinical psychologist, author and political commentator Mary Trump
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrats start plotting as civil war breaks out among Republicans | Politics Weekly America

articles.description:
Donald Trump signed a proclamation on Thursday that he says will turn the Oval Office and the adjacent Cabinet Room into national monuments. The declaration will reportedly prohibit any future presidents from tearing down or making major modifications to the Oval Office or Cabinet Room without approval of Congress. Since returning to office, the US president has transformed the Oval Office with gold accents and statuettes, portraits of famous Americans pulled from storage and a copy of the Declaration of Independence that hangs on the wall.

The redesign has drawn criticism, including from the former president Barack Obama, who recently joked that 'he’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. Just gold everywhere.'

Trump signs proclamation to try to prevent changes to gold-covered Oval Office

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump signs order to make Oval Office a national monument – video

articles.description:
Nithya Raman declared victory in the Los Angeles mayoral race after the incumbent, Karen Bass, conceded. Raman vowed to 'build housing that people can afford, parks for our children to play in, a transit system that can get people where they need to go, a city that is safe for its working people and its families'.

Democratic socialist Nithya Raman wins Los Angeles mayoral race over incumbent Karen Bass


 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman defeats Karen Bass to win Los Angeles mayoral race  – video

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Minister says Labour hoping to offer bed to every rough sleeper in England but cites chronic housing shortage
Andy Burnham’s pledge to tackle rough sleeping by getting “everyone in for Christmas” is in jeopardy amid rising numbers of people on the streets and a severe housing shortage.
Official figures show an increase of nearly 1,000 people sleeping rough in England between January and June, the latest month for which figures are available.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham’s homelessness pledge to ‘get everyone in for Christmas’ in jeopardy

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Coffee shop chain targets growth north of London with extra 500 outlets in big boost for youth employment
Starbucks has set out plans to hire 7,500 new baristas over the next five years, in a boost to youth employment as the chain pins hopes for future growth on the north of the country.
The US coffee shop chain, which employs more than 18,000 people in the UK, said the hiring spree would focus on the Midlands, north of England, Wales and Scotland, as it targets growth north of the M25.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Starbucks plans to hire 7,500 staff in major UK expansion plan

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Jessica Murray; produced by Ivor Manley ; executive producer Eli Block
articles.description:
A crisis in post-adoption support in England is making some adoptive parents feel they have nowhere to turn when things go wrong. Jessica Murray reports
In 2013, Victoria adopted two young children, a brother and a sister. At first everything seemed to be going well. But as he grew older, her son’s behaviour became increasingly extreme.
‘I was not in any way, shape or form prepared for the significant level of trauma that the two children that I adopted were dealing with,’ she told Helen Pidd.
If you are struggling with an adoption, the support group Patch offers help
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The parents who return their adopted children to care – podcast

articles.author: Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
‘Time to throw myself into something new,’ 32-year-old presenter announces on social media while hailing her ‘unforgettable time’ on the show
Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of Love Island after three years.
The 32-year-old presenter of the reality TV show made the announcement on Instagram.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Maya Jama steps down as Love Island host after nine seasons

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Stroke Association says widespread lack of rehabilitation hinders patients’ chances of regaining physical and mental function
Fewer than one in 15 stroke survivors are getting the amount of therapy the NHS should provide to maximise their chances of recovery, a report has revealed.
The figure was a “damning” indictment of the widespread lack of rehabilitation for patients, which was hindering their chances of regaining physical and mental function, the Stroke Association said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Only 6.4% of stroke survivors receive enough therapy, finds ‘damning’ report

articles.author: Richard Adams Education editor
articles.description:
Lucy Powell says proposals to end widespread practice will be included in overhaul of England’s national curriculum 
Pushing GCSE subjects on younger pupils risks turning England’s secondary schools into “early exam factories”, the education secretary has said, warning that it is increasing disengagement from education.
Lucy Powell wants schools to end the widespread practice of teaching GCSE topics to pupils in year 9 or earlier, before they officially start in year 10, and says she plans to reduce the amount of GCSE content to make it easier to fit into the official timetable.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Teaching GCSE topics younger risks turning schools into ‘early exam factories’, Powell warns

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
£40m scheme in England aims to keep most vulnerable people well at home and avoid unnecessary hospital stays 
Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable patients in England are to receive extra support from their GP as part of a £40m drive aimed at keeping them out of hospital this winter.
As the NHS gears up for the pressures of the coming months, family doctors will offer 300,000 people with frailty and long-term conditions health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests designed to prevent avoidable hospital admissions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: GPs to offer 300,000 patients extra support to ease winter strain on NHS

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
Culture secretary says there is still a problem with exploitation and abuse in the industry and public life
The culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, has said there is still a problem with exploitation and abuse in the media industry and a failure to properly deal with allegations after Russell Brand’s conviction for rape and sexual assault.
She said women who came forward were too often not protected by institutions across public life, including in politics, and that huge power imbalances meant speaking up came at a very heavy cost.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russell Brand case must be wake-up call to protect women in media, Lisa Nandy says

articles.author: Sirin Kale in Kilkenny
articles.description:
Two people arrested after Robinson’s presence inflames tensions in scenes witnessed by many on social media
Two people were arrested at an influencer boxing event that descended into a riot in Ireland after the presence of the far-right activist Tommy Robinson inflamed tensions in the crowd.
The riot took place at about midnight on Saturday at an event organised by the controversial internet personality HSTikkyTokky, whose real name is Harrison Sullivan, at the Hub events venue in Kilkenny.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Riot breaks out at influencer boxing event attended by Tommy Robinson in Ireland

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
Culture secretary pushes back against talk of revisiting Brexit but says closer ties would fulfil referendum promises
One of Andy Burnham’s cabinet ministers has said she wants to avoid “circular arguments” about whether the UK should rejoin the EU, underlining divisions at the top of government over revisiting Brexit.
Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, appeared to suggest she was not in favour of rejoining the trade bloc, but she said the prime minister should still pursue closer ties to fulfil the promises made at the time of the referendum.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lisa Nandy wary of ‘circular arguments’ about rejoining EU

articles.author: Kiran Stacey and Sandra Laville
articles.description:
Prime minister says he’s committed to meeting climate targets, but some believe his actions suggest otherwise

Labour expected to cut EV targets for car industry despite MPs’ climate concerns

Andy Burnham insists he is committed to the green transition, but his MPs worry that in decision after decision, he is showing that other priorities come first.
“Our changing climate is a major concern for many Britons, not least because we have just emerged from our hottest summer on record,” the prime minister wrote in the Guardian in September.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Climate always comes second: are green issues slipping down Burnham’s agenda?

articles.author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
Physiotherapy services hit particularly hard compared with other areas of healthcare such as nursing, union finds
Almost half of the NHS trusts in England have no earmarked funding to cover staff on maternity leave, according to analysis that raises fresh concerns about pressure on physiotherapy services.
Freedom of information requests sent to the trusts by the Chartered Society of Physiotherapy (CSP) found that 49% had neither a dedicated budget nor a policy to permit overspending to pay for maternity cover.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Half of NHS trusts in England lack funds earmarked to cover maternity leave

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
Scheme in Derry aims to sow confidence by getting people with learning and physical disabilities into wrestling
The music thumped, the lights blazed and from the ring the announcer did a countdown. “Who is ready to rumble?” he roared. The bellows and cheers indicated that the crowd at St Columb’s Hall in Derry on Saturday night was more than ready for the Foyle Rumble, and so began a wrestling extravaganza of heroes and villains in leotards, masks and kneepads.
The blend of athleticism and scripted storytelling would have been familiar to fans of WrestleMania, but this Northern Irish version came with a twist: many of the performers have learning or physical disabilities, and the characters they play in the ring do not quite stay in the ring.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘No matter what, he doesn’t quit’: disabled wrestlers draw strength from ring alter egos

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll and Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Five of seven facilities in England and Wales never reached operational stage as Tories vacillated over plans to check goods
The UK wasted at least £100m in taxpayers’ money to set up zombie Brexit border inspection posts that were never used, it has been revealed.
The overall cost of Brexit was put at an estimated £4.7bn by the National Audit Office last year but this included years-long transformation of the software used for customs declarations and other systems built to cope with the UK leaving the single market.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK spent £100m on zombie Brexit border inspection posts

articles.author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
articles.description:
See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives
African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.
See My World, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
MPs, local authorities, lawyers, schools and more are receiving floods of grievances, requests and legal challenges, often complex to read and respond to
‘It started as a trickle in 2024 and now it’s an onslaught.” Hollie Wickens, a senior caseworker in a Labour MP’s office, is explaining the daily reality of dealing with surging volumes of artificial intelligence-generated correspondence.
“Half the emails we receive are some form of AI,” she says, adding that this has made requests and complaints much more complex and time-consuming to read and deal with, despite her decade of experience in the role. “It is definitely more taxing.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘AI clog’: UK public bodies battle onslaught of chatbot-generated complaints

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event
Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event.
High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body. In the Dominican Republic, farmers are expected to face drought conditions, with forecasts of drier and warmer than usual conditions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Banana producers in Latin America want better pay to cope with effects of climate crisis

articles.author: Sammy Gecsoyler
articles.description:
David Lammy among those raising concerns after errors found in rejected applications for indefinite leave to remain
Concerns have been raised over the sudden rise in number of Turkish nationals facing removal from the UK as a result of mistakes, prompting accusations that the Home Office has failed to learn the lessons of the Windrush scandal.
Since the start of the year, there has been a sharp rise in the number of rejected applications for indefinite leave to remain for those on European Community Association Agreement (ECAA) visas, a longstanding route to residency for Turkish nationals seeking to set up a business in the UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Windrush’ accusations over sharp rise in Turkish nationals facing removal from UK

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
A lifestyle podcast or brief TV clip is less taxing than a full press conference – but No 10 insists the PM is not ducking accountability 
In an interview this week Andy Burnham said he believed the traditional media was less relevant and the world was “not like that any more”. But some people are now asking: does this change in approach mean less scrutiny?
The question was in part prompted by Burnham’s decision to travel to the Commonwealth heads of government meeting (Chogm) without the usual accompanying pack of reporters, instead bringing just one TV crew and a news agency journalist.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Does Andy Burnham’s pivot from press to social media put scrutiny at risk?

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Twelve midwife-led maternity units have closed in England since 2019 with six closing since Labour came to power in 2024
NHS officials are shutting growing numbers of birth centres in a “shocking” denial of a woman’s right to have a midwife rather than a doctor oversee their baby’s birth, say campaigners.
Twelve birth centres – midwife-led maternity units – have closed in England since 2019. Birth centres play a key role in ensuring that women can choose whether to have their baby at a unit in a hospital run by doctors, at one where midwives are in charge, or at home.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rise in NHS birth centre closures ‘shocking’ denial of women’s rights, experts say

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels and Sammy Gecsoyler
articles.description:
Germany, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg and Denmark say cooperation on clean energy will benefit both sides
Five European leaders have called for closer ties with Britain ahead of a keenly anticipated EU-UK summit.
The leaders of Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg and Denmark, said deeper cooperation on clean energy would benefit both sides in a letter to Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Five European leaders call for closer EU-UK ties ahead of Brussels summit

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Charges against party members and off-piste remarks highlight problems brought about by rapid expansion
Speaking to reporters after unveiling his new defence spokesperson this week, Nigel Farage’s jovial and upbeat mood suddenly switched. Why, he was asked, was a Reform UK councillor who was arrested in January over multiple alleged sexual offences still in his role nearly 10 months later?
“I have no idea,” Farage replied icily. “I was told yesterday, and I wasn’t very happy.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Vetting candidates is a tricky process but Reform can’t seem to get it right

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
The company has lost 182,000 broadband and 644,000 mobile customers in  two years and is operating in an increasingly competitive market competition
Mike Fries may be totting up swingeing job cuts, a £22bn debt pile and the loss of hundreds of thousands of customers, but he appears to be putting a brave face on the situation. “In our minds, anyway, this is not a crisis,” the boss of the co-owner of Virgin Media O2 said this week.
The UK telecoms company, which offers broadband, TV, landline and mobile services, had just announced £800m in cost savings, including potentially cutting up to a quarter of staff. Fries, the chief executive of Liberty Global, faced searching questions on its future and a potential refinancing of its huge debt pile next year. “We made it clear, we have nothing to add to where we sit today,” he said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Job cuts, lost customers and a £22bn debt pile: what has gone wrong at Virgin Media O2?

articles.author: Presented by Aditya Chakrabortty with Nesrine Malik, produced by Frankie Tobi and Luke John Smith, the executive producers were Maz Ebtehaj, Kirsty Major and James Tindale
articles.description:
Today’s political conversation is dominated by one topic above all: race. The Guardian columnist Nesrine Malik has been way ahead of the pack in diagnosing how immigrants, their children and grandchildren are reshaping not just politics but western societies. On the latest episode of Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty, Nesrine talks about where never-ending culture wars in the west and real wars in the Middle East have left people of colour.

Watch more episodes of Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty here
Aditya’s suggested reading list for Nesrine Malik:
In this podcast, Nesrine and I talk about how Gaza has reshaped politics in Britain and America. I quote from this column by her from November 2023 and also cite this prescient piece on Gaza and Labour, from October 2023.
We also discuss “identity politics” (a term only ever used against ethnic minorities). Her book We Need New Stories: Challenging the Toxic Myths Behind Our Age of Discontent is worth revisiting.
More recently, she has addressed the obits being written for Woke 1.0.
Finally, we didn’t get a chance to discuss Sudan’s civil war, but Nesrine’s Long Read on the Khartoum in which she grew up is very powerful.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why Woke 2.0 is taking on Trump and establishment politics | Nesrine Malik | Radical Thinking podcast

articles.author: Rupert Jones
articles.description:
Many experts think fixed rate on 30-month term will still look good after Bank of England raised base rate
A savings account paying “market-leading” 5.3% interest was launched this week by Nationwide building society. It’s only for Nationwide members – but there are more than 19 million of them.
The account was launched just a couple of days before the Bank of England pushed up the main base rate to 4%, a move that will be welcomed by many savers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nationwide launches savings account with ‘market leading’ 5.3% interest

articles.author: Vikram Dodd and Emine Sinmaz
articles.description:
Met police chief says ‘many more’ victims could come forward, as actor and comedian awaits sentencing 
Police are bracing themselves for more victims of Russell Brand to come forward, with at least 10 more women suspected of having been attacked by the disgraced star.
Brand, 51, will be sentenced on Monday to what is expected to be a lengthy jail sentence for rape and sexual assaults after he abused his fame to become a “predator” targeting women, and got away with it for years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russell Brand suspected to have attacked at least 10 other women

articles.author: Mark Sweney and Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
Asian and European markets follow US tech rout with many analysts predicting more waves of selling to come
European and Asian stock markets fell sharply on Friday after the Democrats’ decisive victory in the midterms triggered a rout in US tech stocks a day earlier.
A sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday was followed by sharp falls in Asian stock markets on Friday. The investor sentiment then reached London, where the market was, at one stage, poised for its worst day since March.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Global stocks fall amid ‘big worries over AI’ after Democrats’ midterms triumph

articles.author: Ian Sample Science editor
articles.description:
The most enjoyable conversations strike a balance between exploring a topic and pulling in fresh ideas, study finds
As an early stab at rules for conversation, Cicero did a fine job: watch your tone, never look bored, never lose your temper and never ramble on, particularly about yourself, he advised.
Now scientists have followed in the great orator’s footsteps and discovered a telltale signature of an enjoyable chinwag. The secret of a mutually satisfying exchange is a healthy dose of pink noise, they say.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Want to have a better chat? Scientists say the secret is ‘pink noise’

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Lisa Nandy calls for whistleblowers to be protected and highlights bravery of women who came forward in case
Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, has warned that Russell Brand’s conviction for rape and sexual assault must be a “wake-up call” to the media world and beyond, after widespread concerns over the failures to confront his behaviour.
With renewed calls from TV insiders for a new examination of how Brand’s treatment of women was tolerated for so long, Nandy said the case was a “defining moment for our country”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russell Brand rape conviction must be ‘wake-up call’, says culture secretary

articles.author: Chris Osuh, Aamna Mohdin and Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Some relatives of British citizens say they feel left behind, but announcement has brought relief to many care workers
“The only time we’re regarded as human beings is when they need a lot of hands onboard, like during Covid. But after that, we’re tossed away like we’re some rubbish,” Aneisha Williams says.
Williams, 39, was months from qualifying for indefinite leave to remain after 10 years in the UK. But claiming housing benefit could delay her settlement for years under Shabana Mahmood’s “earned settlement” plans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I feel free now’: Shabana Mahmood’s immigration shake-up provokes mixed emotions

articles.author: Pippa Neill
articles.description:
Mild autumn temperatures causing premature flowering and raising concerns for pollinators, say experts
Trees are experiencing an “early spring” because of mild UK temperatures this autumn, with experts warning this could cause long-term harm to pollinators.
Last month was warmer than average across all parts of the UK, with October marking the ninth consecutive month with above-average mean temperatures.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Everything is so out of whack’: UK trees experience spring six months early

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Emine Sinmaz; produced by Saskia Collette and May Robson; executive producer Homa Khaleeli
articles.description:
In the decades he’s spent on screens, Russell Brand’s been a comedian, an actor, a presenter and a political anarchist.
Now he has been convicted of rape and sexual assaults.
Emine Sinmaz reports
We’ve seen many iterations of Russell Brand. Camp Camden goth. Outrageous standup and TV host. Hollywood star. Political anarchist. Reborn Christian conspiracy theorist.
Brand always wanted to be famous. And when he attained celebrity in the 2000s, he was seen as a breath of fresh air. Hyper-camp, hyper-sexual, hyper-articulate, he was considered edgy by TV and radio commissioners and funnier than anyone else by his fans. A Guardian columnist and the Sun’s shagger of the year, Brand was supposed to be ironic, a pop culture provocateur, journalist Sophie Heawood tells Nosheen Iqbal. But in the past decade, it’s become harder to remember why he was so celebrated.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The crimes of Russell Brand - podcast

In the decades he’s spent on our screens, Russell Brand’s been a comedian, an actor, a presenter and a political anarchist. Now he has been convicted of rape and sexual assaults. Emine Sinmaz reports
